title: Wartime Farming — Roads, Railroads, and the Dehydration Plant
description: Roads improved, allowing farmers to transport milk and livestock to the railroad. During WW1 and WW2, local farmers provided potatoes to the evaporation/dehydration plant, which packed the processed potatoes into sealed cans and dropped them from planes to feed Allied forces. After the wars, Heber Hatfield began the potato chip factory, which always had a local market for different grades of potatoes.
